findings.summary: Host enforcement is not yet proven by live readback: branch protection or an active ruleset must require the stable check name `loom-pr-merge-gate` on `main`, and the proof should be captured as fresh evidence before claiming “host-enforced” closure.

disposition.summary: Complete Phase 3: enable/verify required check via live host readback and record the evidence in the WI-763 fact chain / host proof artifacts.

findings.details: Spec/plan explicitly defer host mutation, but closure still requires live readback proof; workflow presence alone is not sufficient.

findings.summary: `.loom/reviews/WI-763.json` remains a scaffold (`decision: fallback`, placeholder reviewer/validation summary), so `checkpoint merge` / `pr-gate` will fail closed until a real authored review record is recorded and bound to the current `latest_validation_summary` and reviewed head (carrier-only drift allowed).

disposition.summary: Record this formal review result into `.loom/reviews/WI-763.json` with `decision: allow`, correct `reviewer`, and freshness bindings (reviewed head + reviewed validation summary).

findings.details: This is expected before opening the PR / attempting to satisfy the new gate, but it must be completed for the system to work end-to-end.

findings.summary: The required check workflow checks out and executes repo code at the PR head (`python3 tools/loom_flow.py ...`). This is acceptable for trusted contributor sets, but it increases risk if untrusted PRs can run the required check with a read-scoped token.

disposition.summary: Document contributor trust assumptions for enabling this required check, or redesign the gate to avoid executing arbitrary PR code (e.g., validate via API-fetched artifacts / pinned tooling).

findings.details: Current workflow permissions are read-only, but executing PR code is still a meaningful boundary that should be made explicit.

findings.summary: `controlled-merge` verifies enforcement via branch protection required status contexts; it does not currently read GitHub rulesets. Also, the workflow triggers only on `pull_request` (not `merge_group`), so merge-queue usage may require an explicit compatibility decision.

disposition.summary: Either (a) scope enforcement verification to branch protection only and document it, or (b) add ruleset readback support; confirm whether `merge_group` support is needed for the repo’s merge strategy.

findings.details: Without this, host enforcement may be misreported (rulesets) and merge queue may be unintentionally blocked if enabled while the check is required.
